analogy.rationale: F10 (factor Xa) is a coagulation protease whose expression and activity are largely restricted to hepatocytes and the vasculature; the nine cell lines are unlikely to express a functional coagulation cascade, so coagulation factor inhibitors should elicit little to no transcriptional response. Vitamin K antagonists act on the same coagulation pathway (via VKORC1) and are the closest mechanistic neighbor, while the other listed classes are unrelated and included only as low-similarity comparators.
